decisions.finding: QDR 4Q8a/4Q8b and Qumran-Digital 4Q8a/4Q8b refer to different displayed content. Four content/locator correspondences are now explicitly recorded rather than silently treating the index's exact labels as identities.
decisions.counterargument: Similar biblical words alone could occur on different copies. Line/preservation-layout correspondence strengthens the catalogue lead but is not independent image or inventory verification.
decisions.next_gate: Trace these content units through DJD XII and present IAA plate/fragment identifiers; do not merge the two QDR records merely because Qumran-Digital places them under 4Q8.

decisions.literary_assignment: Kings versus Isaiah unresolved by this pass
decisions.finding: Both current pages cross-reference the other label in each of four main lines and the same PAM sub-locator. Publisher subtitle presents Kings or Isaiah alternatives. They must not be counted as two independent supports.
decisions.counterargument: Reciprocal publication references establish an editorial equivalence, not a new physical inspection or resolution of the parallel Kings/Isaiah text's literary identity.
decisions.next_gate: Read Puech2012 pp469-472 and inspect exact PAM/IAA image location before adopting a physical identifier or literary assignment.

decisions.finding: Tigchelaar2023's publisher subtitle explicitly challenges both separate labels in favor of 4Q29 frag.3. Qumran-Digital still lists them in 2026; the website date cannot overrule the named 2023 challenge.
decisions.counterargument: Title alone does not provide the image argument, exact fragment extent, or reception of the reassignment. Current 4Q29 page groups fragment3 with other fragments; it does not isolate physical boundaries for us.
decisions.next_gate: Obtain authorized full text pp121-122 and the compared photographs. Keep separate catalogue records but suppress unreviewed independent-witness promotion.

decisions.finding: Record2 has f1 lines1-3 and f2 lines1-2; record209 has f1 lines4-5. Distinct hashes and disjoint f1 line numbers contradict a byte-duplicate explanation, but do not prove two manuscripts or a safe merge.
decisions.published_comparison: Qumran-Digital has f1 lines1-3 and f2 lines1-2. Its f1 subdued/earth snippets correspond to QDR record2 f1 lines2-3, not matching line numbers. QDR record2 includes extensive supplied Gen1:27-28 and Gen1:9-10 contexts; record209's Gen1:29 contexts are largely supplied. These reference tags cannot be counted as preserved verse coverage.
decisions.counterargument: Record209 could be continuation material from the same editorial unit, but its provenance and relation to the current edition remain unverified. Disjoint numbering alone neither authenticates nor invalidates it.
decisions.next_gate: Check source-conversion history and the relevant published edition/photographs. Any downstream extraction must retain ordinal2 versus209.

decisions.finding: Miller2017's publisher abstract names 4Q103a (4QProvc) separately from 4Q103 (4QProvb). The Qumran-Digital index's missing label therefore cannot become a claim that 4Q103a is unattested. QDR record167 covers two small fragment units tagged Prov9:16-17 and10:30-32; the consulted Qumran-Digital 4Q103 page does not give an explicit equivalence to them.
decisions.counterargument: A publication mentioning the label does not authenticate the two particular QDR fragment assignments. We have not verified whether record167 combines material differently from the later edition.
decisions.next_gate: Verify both QDR fragment assignments against DJD XVI and later 4Q103a studies before accepting an alias or counting preserved verses.
